description: The provided chart is a donut-style pie chart illustrating the relative emphasis or scoring of various capabilities or components within a system, likely related to language model behavior as suggested by the paper title “Can Language Models Follow Multiple Turns of Entangled Instructions.” The chart is divided into ten outer segments, each labeled with a capability and an associated numerical value, and four inner segments representing higher-level functional categories: “Contradiction Resolution,” “Context Tracking,” “Context Retrieving,” and an unlabeled central white circle. The outer segments, arranged clockwise from the top-left, are: “Prioritization” (100, light red), “Personalization” (100, red-orange), “Privacy Protection” (111, dark red — though the label is partially obscured), “Multitasking” (160, green — the largest segment), “Dynamic Instruction” (100, light cyan), “Memorization” (100, cyan), “Dynamic Environment” (100, dark blue), “Recursive Reasoning” (110, medium blue), “Triggering” (100, light blue), and “Prioritization” again (100, light red — appears duplicated). The inner ring segments are color-coded to group related outer segments: “Contradiction Resolution” (brownish-red) encompasses “Personalization” and “Privacy Protection”; “Context Tracking” (dark blue) covers “Recursive Reasoning,” “Dynamic Environment,” and “Triggering”; “Context Retrieving” (dark green) includes “Multitasking,” “Dynamic Instruction,” and “Memorization”; and the central white circle may represent a core or foundational layer. The values suggest a scoring or weighting system, with “Multitasking” receiving the highest score (160), followed by “Privacy Protection” (111) and “Recursive Reasoning” (110), while most others are normalized at 100. The chart visually emphasizes the centrality of context management and multitasking in handling entangled instructions.
